dataset_domain: AgroVision AI Sample Image Quality & Evaluation Registry

samples.suspected_disease: Tomato Late Blight Fruit Rot / Anthracnose
samples.visible_symptoms: Large sunken dark-brown/black necrotic rot lesion at the calyx/stem attachment spreading onto the fruit shoulder; green foliage in background
possible_alternative_diagnoses: Tomato Late Blight Fruit Rot (Phytophthora infestans)
samples.label_source: Provisional visual interpretation / Unverified web image
samples.verification_notes: Depicts tomato fruit with necrotic rot rather than foliar blight. Organ is fruit, whereas model training dataset for Tomato Late Blight consists of foliar leaflets. Pathogen cannot be definitively confirmed without microbiological culture or source provenance.
samples.expected_prediction: Abstain / Organ Mismatch / Tomato Late Blight

samples.suspected_disease: Tomato Fruit Spots (Ghost Spot / Early Blight / Anthracnose)
samples.visible_symptoms: Multiple brownish sunken spots and circular necrotic speckling across unripe green/yellow tomato fruit skins
samples.label_source: Provisional visual interpretation / Unverified web image
samples.verification_notes: Depicts green tomato fruits with extensive circular pitting/speckling. Affected plant organ is fruit. Since the dataset classes represent foliar diseases, fruit lesions represent out-of-distribution or cross-organ manifestations. Specific pathogen unverified.

samples.visible_symptoms: Dark brown-to-black discolored spikelets and necrotic grains on emerging green-yellow rice panicle
possible_alternative_diagnoses: Glume Blight / Grain Discoloration (Bipolaris oryzae / Curvularia lunata)
samples.label_source: Provisional visual interpretation / Unverified web image
samples.verification_notes: Depicts rice reproductive panicle with grain glume discoloration. The model's Rice Blast class was predominantly trained on leaf blast lesions. Grain discoloration and panicle blast have distinct visual morphology. Ground-truth pathogen unverified.
samples.expected_prediction: Abstain / Rice Blast / Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight

samples.visible_symptoms: Characteristic enlarged velvety greenish-black smut balls (pseudomorphs) replacing individual grains on ripening rice panicle
samples.verification_notes: Symptom morphology is unambiguous for Rice False Smut (Ustilaginoidea virens). However, False Smut is NOT present in the 72-class model or Phase 2 disease registry (which includes Rice Blast, Brown Spot, Leaf Smut, Sheath Blight, Bacterial Blight, Tungro, Leaf Scald). The model must not hallucinate a supported disease with high confidence; it should safely abstain.

samples.scientific_name: Unconfirmed fungal ear rot / secondary pest damage
samples.visible_symptoms: Exposed ear of corn with husk opened at the middle/tip, showing yellow kernels with localized dark necrotic/black kernel rot and insect damage
possible_alternative_diagnoses: Corn Earworm (Helicoverpa zea) injury with secondary rot
samples.label_source: Provisional visual interpretation / Shutterstock stock photo
samples.verification_notes: Depicts a maize ear/cob rather than maize foliage. Model classes for Corn are strictly foliar (Common Rust, Northern Leaf Blight, Cercospora Gray Leaf Spot). Kernel damage may be primary insect injury followed by opportunistic saprophytes. Pathogen unconfirmed.

samples.scientific_name: Insect injury (likely Spodoptera frugiperda / Fall Armyworm)
samples.visible_symptoms: Severe foliar chewing injury: large ragged holes, window-paning, and lamina tears held by a human hand, without chlorotic or fungal sporulation halos
samples.label_source: Diagnostic morphological inspection (chewing patterns vs microbial lesion)
samples.verification_notes: Classic mechanical/insect mastication damage (chewed leaf blade). It is NOT a microbial disease. Must not be classified as Common Rust or Northern Leaf Blight. The model should abstain due to low disease feature confidence.

samples.suspected_disease: Soybean Foliar Necrosis (Sudden Death Syndrome / Brown Spot / Target Spot)
samples.scientific_name: Glycine max foliar pathogen (Fusarium virguliforme / Septoria glycines / Corynespora cassiicola)
samples.visible_symptoms: Trifoliate ovate pubescent leaflets with prominent interveinal necrotic brown blotches bordered by chlorotic yellow margins
samples.label_source: Botanical leaflet morphology (trifoliate pubescent leaflet) & lesion inspection
samples.verification_notes: Botanical morphology clearly indicates Soybean (Glycine max). While PlantVillage had 'Soybean___healthy', diseased soybean classes were excluded from the unified 72-class crop disease model. The system must not force this image into Chilli, Tomato, or Grape.

samples.visible_symptoms: Linear parallel stripes of bright yellow-orange powdery pustules (urediniospores) aligned along leaf veins of cereal blades, flanked by chlorosis
possible_alternative_diagnoses: Wheat Leaf Rust (Puccinia triticina) - though linear striping is diagnostic for stripe rust
Barley Stripe Rust (Puccinia striiformis f. sp. hordei)
samples.label_source: Educational agricultural guide illustration & characteristic linear pustule morphology
samples.verification_notes: Definitive morphological manifestation of Stripe Rust / Yellow Rust on wheat foliage. Linear parallel stripe formation is pathognomonic for Puccinia striiformis on Poaceae. This class exists in the 72-class model ('Wheat___Stripe_rust') and Phase 2 registry ('dis_wheat_stripe_rust').

samples.suspected_disease: Wheat Stem Rust (Black Rust) / Leaf Rust
samples.scientific_name: Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici / Puccinia triticina
samples.visible_symptoms: Dense reddish-brown to dark brown erumpent pustules erupting across cereal stems and drying leaf sheaths/blades
possible_alternative_diagnoses: Wheat Stem Rust (Puccinia graminis) - predominant on culms
Wheat Leaf Rust (Puccinia triticina) - on foliage
samples.label_source: Agricultural extension field publication on cereal rusts
samples.verification_notes: Definitive cereal rust on wheat stems/leaves. In the unified model, wheat rust classes include 'Wheat___Leaf_rust' and 'Wheat___Stripe_rust'. Stem rust is not a distinct class in the model (often absorbed into leaf rust or out-of-class). The crop is verified as Wheat, and the pathogen is verified as Puccinia rust complex.
samples.expected_prediction: Wheat Leaf Rust or Wheat Stripe Rust
